heading: INT. SUDSY'S 24-HOUR CAR WASH, TUNNEL BAY - NIGHT

units.text: INT. SUDSY'S 24-HOUR CAR WASH, TUNNEL BAY - NIGHT
Brushes hang like giant sleeping spiders.
Neon pink water pools on the concrete.
A radio plays soft country from a plastic shelf.
The tunnel is empty.
THE MAN, forties, in a camel coat and gloves, enters on foot from the rain, a briefcase held tight against his chest.
He glances at the exit, then at the cash window.
DUKE, sixty, the night attendant, sits on an upturned bucket with a thermos between his knees, doing a crossword.
RHODA FENWICK, thirties, in a navy suit with a lanyard that says CITY INSPECTOR, steps out of the office with a clipboard, pen already uncapped.
Duke fills in a word and looks up.
The Man edges along the wall, trying to keep out of the light.
Rhoda follows him with her eyes, then with her pen, and writes something on the clipboard, and walks toward him at an even pace.
Evening. You here for a wash?
units.name: RHODA

units.text: I walked.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: That's an odd way to get a car washed.
units.name: RHODA

units.text: I'm between cars.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: Duke pours coffee into the thermos cap and drinks.
He doesn't take his eyes off the briefcase.
Eleven letters. "Unwelcome visitor."
units.name: DUKE

units.text: Trespasser.
units.name: RHODA

units.text: That's ten.
units.name: DUKE

units.text: Intruder. Eight. Well, I tried.
units.name: RHODA

units.text: The Man lets the briefcase drop to his side.
It swings, heavy, and thuds against his knee.
Rhoda's pen stops.
Sir, what's your name?
units.name: RHODA

units.text: Does it matter?
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: I like to put a name on my forms.
units.name: RHODA

units.text: Boone.
units.name: THE MAN

units.text: Duke chuckles into his thermos.
Boone like Daniel?
units.name: DUKE

units.text: Boone like Walter. Walter Boone.
units.name: BOONE

units.text: Rhoda writes it down.
Duke fills in four more squares of the puzzle.
Boone sets the briefcase on the floor and slides it, with his foot, a few inches toward the drain.
Mr. Boone, would you open that for me?
units.name: RHODA

units.text: It's just papers.
units.name: BOONE

units.text: Then it won't take a minute.
units.name: RHODA

units.text: Boone looks at Duke.
Duke looks at the crossword.
Boone kneels, thumbs the latches, and lifts the lid.
Inside, stacked in rubber bands, is a thick wall of cash.
Rhoda lowers the clipboard and says nothing for a long moment.
That's a lot of papers.
units.name: RHODA

units.text: I'm a very organized man.
units.name: BOONE

units.text: Duke drains his thermos, caps it, and rises with a grunt.
He slides a squeegee off its rack and holds it like a cane.
Seven across. "Fair deal."
units.name: DUKE

units.text: Hush.
units.name: RHODA

units.text: Eight letters. Starts with a G.
units.name: DUKE

units.text: Boone and Rhoda both turn to stare at him.
